title: Assessment of Differences in the Anthropometric, Physiological and Training Characteristics of Finishers and Non-finishers in a Tropical 161-km Ultra-marathon
authors: Tan PL, Tan FH, Bosch AN
population: Runners entered in a tropical 161-km race; 12 finishers and 14 non-finishers, tested at least 3 weeks before the race with training logged from 6 weeks before.
findings: 26 runners (12 finishers, 14 non-finishers); training sessions were recorded from six weeks before the race.
Effect-size calculations showed moderate differences between finishers and non-finishers in longest run attempted (ES = 0.73, P = 0.07), so the difference did not reach P < 0.05.
Other differences: cross-training hours (ES = 0.73, P = 0.06), lactate concentration at LT1 (ES = 0.88, P = 0.05), velocity at LT2 (ES = 0.70, P = 0.07).
The abstract gives no longest-run values in km or minutes. Authors conclude runners should not neglect long runs and should incorporate cross-training.
limitations: Tiny sample, many comparisons, no result at P < 0.05 for longest run, six-week training window only, no longest-run values or threshold in the abstract.
implications: Weak, non-significant hint that a longer longest run goes with finishing at 161 km; supports keeping a long-run target but gives no minute or km threshold, so it cannot calibrate 240 or 270 min.
Grade C at most for any long-run parameter citing this paper (D for a number); do not use it to justify a number.

verification.notes: Re-fetched Crossref (title, 2017, Int J Exerc Sci, first author Tan) and the Europe PMC abstract (PMID 28966704). N=12/14, ES and P values for longest run, cross-training, LT1 and LT2 match. Reworded finding 2 to say the abstract calls the differences moderate and that longest run did not reach P < 0.05.
